ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the top of the figure is a phosphoryl chloride fragment, with P as the center, connected to O above, connected to Cl on the left, right, and below, and with curved arrows; in the middle is an amide/carbonyl bridge, containing C=O, a carbonyl carbon connected to N, and N connected to the right aromatic ring; below there are two aromatic rings, the left aromatic ring bearing R and R1 substituents, and the right aromatic ring connected to the carbon skeleton attached to N. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, ignore all curved arrows, count only non-hydrogen bonds, and count by partition according to the specified method. The two benzene rings together contribute 12 bond units. The remaining phosphorus/amide/connection part: P=O counts as 2, three P-Cl single bonds count as 3, totaling 5; carbonyl C=O counts as 2, carbonyl C-N, carbonyl C-aromatic ring, and N-right aromatic ring each count as 1, totaling 5. Therefore the non-aromatic-ring part totals 10. Total number = 12 + 10 = 22.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and split the drawing into the top phosphorus fragment, the middle amide/carbonyl bridge, and the two aromatic rings. Ignore all curved arrows because the prompt says to disregard them. Then count every non-hydrogen bond line exactly once, with each double bond counted as 2. The two benzene rings together contribute 12 bond units, and the remaining explicit non-H bonds in the phosphorus/amide/linker portion contribute 10 more. Adding the subtotals gives 22 total bonds.
